# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Age:** 59 years old  <sub>[v5 c26 P26](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0026)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** The fair Cornelia  <sub>[v5 c23 P40](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0040)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face and jolly brown eyes. She wears a hard little knob of fair hair held on her head by a tight elastic band rather than hat pins. She is described as having a comfortable, matronly figure and does not resemble the traditional old maid.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)_

## Personality

Cornelia is famous for having a bitter tongue and a kind heart. She is extremely outspoken, disdainful of men, and critical of Methodists. She is always ready to sound the alarm where men are concerned and makes a principle of snubbing any men using 'high-falutin' language. Despite her sharp words, she is quick to help anyone in trouble, especially children, and makes a point of submitting to facts once they are settled rather than arguing uselessly.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027), [v4 c26 P3](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0003), [v4 c26 P25](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0025), [v4 c30 P48](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0048), [v5 c23 P78](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0078)_

## History

Cornelia grew up as an only child for eight years until her younger brother was born. Although she had her pick of suitors when she was young, she remained unmarried for many years, nursing a long-standing disdain for men and Methodists while serving as a compassionate neighbor in Four Winds. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, she promptly formed a close friendship with her, frequently visiting to swap stories, sew, and mock local events. She also served as Leslie Moore's best friend, helping her through her hardships and cleaning the gray house up the brook. Cornelia was elected a delegate to the W.F.M.S. convention in Kingsport. Later, she accepted a proposal from Marshall Elliott, whom she married despite his Conservative political stance, remaining Mrs. Marshall Elliott for thirteen years by the time of Glen St. Mary events. When Mary Vance was discovered starving in a barn over-harbour, Cornelia sent her husband to investigate and took Mary into her home, where Mary became a helpful companion. Cornelia also participated actively in the Presbyterian church and Ladies' Aid Society, helping clean the manse and taking in the minister's children when needed.
